title: Gabber equivariant very-tame modification
statement:
Let $C$ be an integral excellent separated Noetherian scheme and $B\subset C$ a nowhere dense closed subset such that $(C,B)$ is a log regular pair. Let a finite group $G$ of order invertible on $C$ act on the pair, generically freely. Put $T=C\setminus U$, where $U$ is the largest invariant open on which $G$ acts freely. There exist an integral Noetherian scheme $C_1$ with an action of $G$, a $G$-equivariant projective morphism $f:C_1\to C$ and a dense open $C^0\subseteq C$ such that $f$ restricts to an isomorphism $f^{-1}(C^0)\to C^0$, and such that, with $B_1=f^{-1}(B\cup T)$, the pair $(C_1,B_1)$ is log regular and the action of $G$ on it is very tame. Moreover $f^{-1}(V)$ is dense in $C_1$ for any dense open $V\subset C$. Separated means that the diagonal into the product over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is a closed immersion.

Here admissible means that each orbit is contained in an affine open; generically free means free on geometric points over a dense invariant open. An action on a pair preserves its closed subset and hence its divisorial log structure. Projective here means that for every affine open $W\subseteq C$ the restriction $f^{-1}(W)\to W$ is projective in the sense of [def-kun-projective]: a closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^N_W$ followed by the projection. The log regular pair and its geometric stalks are those of [def-trf-log-regular-pair].

At a geometric point $\bar c$ of $C_1$, write $A=\mathcal O_{C_1,\bar c}$, $M$ for the divisorial log stalk, $\overline M=M/A^\times$, $I$ for the ideal generated by nonunit log sections, and $H$ for the stabilizer of the geometric point. Very tame means that $|H|$ is prime to the residue characteristic, $H$ acts trivially on $\overline M$, and $H$ acts trivially on $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. In residue characteristic zero the prime-to-characteristic condition is void.

source.place: Expose VIII Theorem 1.1, printed p.85, and IX Theorem 2.3, printed p.134; integral case of the modification construction (normalized blowup towers, VIII sections 4–5). Very tame is VI 3.1, pp.73–74.
